::: {.about-lead}
## Field biologist by training, quantitative ecologist by practice.

I am **Jorge A. Martín-Ávila**, a PhD in Ecology, Biodiversity and Global Change from the University of Alcalá (Spain). My interests lie in the links between **biodiversity, species interactions, landscape ecology, and ecosystem services**.

My work has involved monitoring raptor nests, studying their diet and movements, and using ecological and statistical models to understand how native predators interact with an invasive species. I value research that moves between field observations, rigorous analysis and actionable conservation questions.
:::

## Current work

**Environmental assessment and data analysis — Tragsatec (Spain)**  
My professional work includes ecological data processing, habitat assessment and spatial analysis. I continue to develop my academic research interests and collaborations in parallel.

## Academic background

- **PhD in Ecology, Biodiversity and Global Change** — University of Alcalá, 2025. *Cum laude*, international mention. Thesis: *The role of the honey buzzard in the control of the Asian hornet*.
- **MSc in Animal Biology Research** — University of Alcalá, 2019.
- **BSc in Biology** — University of Alcalá, 2018.

## Research experience

My doctoral research (2021–2025) was supported by a Spanish FPI predoctoral fellowship. I have worked on ecological fieldwork, GPS telemetry, camera-trap monitoring, statistical modelling, scientific writing and interdisciplinary research. My experience includes an international research stay at **Senckenberg** in Frankfurt and university teaching activities.

## Student supervision

I have contributed to the supervision of **nine undergraduate and master's dissertations** (2021–2023), spanning animal ecology, migration, habitat selection, biological invasions and ecological data analysis. My roles include thesis direction and joint supervision.

[Explore supervised dissertations](Supervision.qmd)
